name: Late Bronze Age Canaanite religion (Ugaritic textual horizon)

dating.dating_summary: This entity models the Late Bronze Age Canaanite religious world principally through the unusually rich Ugaritic archive; Ugarit is evidence for that wider Northwest Semitic environment, not a synonym for every local Canaanite cult.

earliest_written_attestation.note: Ugaritic mythic, ritual, pantheon, and administrative texts from the Late Bronze Age provide the principal written horizon used for this seed.

surviving_manuscript_date.note: The cuneiform tablets excavated at Ugarit/Ras Shamra preserve the Late Bronze Age textual corpus.

notes: Do not collapse all Canaanite religion into Ugarit. The Ugaritic corpus is used because it preserves direct Northwest Semitic evidence for El, Baal/Hadad, divine council structures, and mythic language that can be compared with early Israelite religion.

source_links.label: French Ministry of Culture — Ugarit/Ras Shamra
source_links.supports: Archaeological site and Late Bronze Age history; not evidence every Canaanite cult was identical.

source_links.label: University of Chicago — Ras Shamra Tablet Inventory
source_links.supports: Inventory and provenance of tablets; text-by-text claims require further verification.

source_links.label: University of Göttingen — Ugaritic poetic text corpus
source_links.supports: Numbered tablet entries (e.g. KTU 1.1–1.6) and editorial corpus; not a proof of direct borrowing.

public_profile_facts.statement: The Göttingen critical corpus lists the Baal Cycle tablets as KTU 1.1–1.6, a directly identifiable group of Ugaritic mythological texts.
public_profile_facts.evidence_scope: Verified at corpus inventory level. Further passage-level checks are required for specific interpretations or claims of borrowing by other traditions.
